questions.q: What classical code is the Steane code built from?
options: The Hamming(7,4) code's parity-check matrix
The 5-bit repetition code
The classical 3-bit repetition code
A random 7x7 binary matrix with no special structure
questions.explain: The Steane code reuses the classical Hamming(7,4) code's parity-check matrix H to build both its X-type and Z-type stabilizers.

questions.q: What verified property of the Hamming(7,4) parity-check matrix H makes the Steane code construction valid?
options: Self-orthogonality -- every pairwise mod-2 dot product among its 3 rows (including each row with itself) equals 0
Every entry of H is a 1
H is the identity matrix
H has exactly 7 rows
questions.explain: Self-orthogonality was directly verified (all 9 pairwise dot products among the 3 rows, including self-pairs, equal 0 mod 2), which is exactly what guarantees all 6 resulting stabilizers commute with each other.

questions.q: How many stabilizer generators does the Steane code have, and how are they split?
options: 2 total, same as the bit-flip code
9 total, matching the Shor code
3 total, all X-type
6 total: 3 X-type and 3 Z-type, both built from the same 3 rows of H
questions.explain: The Steane code has 6 stabilizer generators (n-k = 7-1 = 6), split evenly into 3 X-type and 3 Z-type, both derived from the same 3 rows of H thanks to self-orthogonality.

questions.q: What does the notation [[7,1,3]] mean for the Steane code?
options: A code requiring exactly 13 total qubits including ancillas
7 logical qubits encoded using 1 physical qubit and 3 ancillas
7 physical qubits, 1 logical qubit, minimum distance 3
7 stabilizer generators, 1 ancilla qubit, 3 correction rounds
questions.explain: Standard [[n,k,d]] stabilizer-code notation: n physical qubits, k logical qubits, and d minimum distance -- here 7, 1, and 3 respectively, meaning it corrects exactly 1 arbitrary single-qubit error.

questions.q: Why is the Steane code's 7-qubit overhead considered an improvement over the Shor code's 9-qubit overhead, given both correct the same arbitrary single-qubit error?
options: It achieves the identical correction power with fewer physical qubits, and additionally supports transversal logical Hadamard, X, Z, and CNOT gates
The Steane code cannot actually correct Z errors, making the comparison invalid
7 qubits is worse than 9, not better, contrary to what the lesson claims
The Shor code and Steane code protect against entirely different error types, so they aren't comparable
questions.explain: Both codes correct any single-qubit Pauli error, but the Steane code does so with 2 fewer physical qubits and has the added fault-tolerance-relevant property of transversal gates, covered further in chapter 7.
